title: Task Assigning Standard
summary: Task assignment clearly allocates responsibilities so everyone knows what needs to be done, who owns it, when it should be completed, and the expected standard.

sections.title: The Standard
paragraphs: Task Assignment is the process of clearly allocating responsibilities to therapists and team members based on the needs of the spa, their roles, schedules, and operational priorities. Effective task assignment ensures that everyone understands what needs to be done, who is responsible, when it should be completed, and the expected standard.

sections.title: 1. Relevance of Task Assigning
paragraphs: Proper task assignment helps Zura Spa maintain order, accountability, efficiency, and teamwork.

items.label: Clarity
items.body: Everyone knows their responsibility and what is expected.

items.label: Accountability
items.body: Tasks have clear ownership, making follow-up easier.

items.label: Efficiency
items.body: Work is distributed appropriately instead of being left to a few people.

items.label: Teamwork
items.body: Staff understand how their individual tasks contribute to the overall operation.

items.label: Consistency
items.body: Important routines and standards are less likely to be forgotten.

items.label: Fairness
items.body: Tasks can be distributed reasonably rather than being repeatedly given to the same individuals.

items.label: Client Experience
items.body: When operational tasks are completed properly, therapists can focus better on delivering quality service.

items.label: Problem Prevention
items.body: Clear assignments reduce confusion, duplication, and the assumption that "someone else will handle it."

sections.title: 2. Therapist's Mindset Towards Assigned Tasks
paragraphs: A therapist should approach an assigned task with the mindset: "If I have been assigned this responsibility, I own it until it is completed or properly handed over."
list: Receive assignments with a positive and responsible attitude.
Understand the task before beginning.
Ask for clarification when instructions are unclear.
Complete tasks according to the required standard, not merely to say they are done.
Manage their time properly.
Take initiative when they notice something that requires attention.
Communicate early if they cannot complete a task.
Avoid waiting to be repeatedly reminded.
Understand that tasks are part of teamwork, not punishment.
Be willing to support the team when operational needs change.
Accept reasonable correction or follow-up professionally.
sections.closing: Don't wait to be chased. Don't assume someone else will do it. Don't do the minimum just to tick a box. Take ownership.

sections.title: 3. What Leaders Should Do
paragraphs: Leaders and supervisors should understand that good task assignment is also good leadership.

sections.title: Give Clear Instructions
paragraphs: Explain exactly what needs to be done, rather than giving vague directions.
Instead of: "Please sort out the room."
Say: "Please reset Room 2, replace the used towels, restock the required supplies, and have it ready before the next session."

sections.title: Set Clear Expectations
paragraphs: Where necessary, communicate the expected quality, deadline, and priority.

sections.title: Assign According to Role and Capacity
paragraphs: Consider the therapist's responsibilities, schedule, workload, ability, and current operational demands.

sections.title: Distribute Tasks Fairly
paragraphs: Avoid repeatedly assigning undesirable tasks to the same individuals without a valid operational reason.

sections.title: Follow Up
paragraphs: Check whether important tasks have been completed without creating unnecessary micromanagement.

sections.title: Provide Support
paragraphs: If a therapist genuinely needs clarification, resources, or assistance, leadership should provide appropriate support.

sections.title: Give Feedback
paragraphs: Recognize good execution and address poor execution promptly and professionally.

sections.title: Lead by Example
paragraphs: Leaders should demonstrate the same accountability, punctuality, discipline, and willingness to contribute that they expect from the team.

sections.title: 4. What Leaders Should Not Do
list: Give unclear or contradictory instructions.
Assign tasks without considering operational priorities.
Constantly overload one person without reason.
Use task assignments as a form of personal punishment.
Show favoritism when distributing responsibilities.
Publicly embarrass a therapist over a task.
Assume that a therapist understands an unclear instruction.
Change instructions repeatedly without communicating the change.
Assign a task and then provide no reasonable opportunity or resources to complete it.
Expect staff to guess priorities.
Micromanage every small action unnecessarily.
Ignore completed work and only point out mistakes.
Allow poor performance to continue without addressing it.
Blame staff for failures caused by unclear instructions.
Use anger, threats, or humiliation as a management method.
Assign responsibility and then take away the person's ability to complete it.
Make promises about tasks or schedules that leadership cannot reasonably keep.

sections.title: 5. The Zura Task Assignment Standard
paragraphs: ASSIGN → CLARIFY → CONFIRM → EXECUTE → FOLLOW UP → ACCOUNT
A leader should ensure the task is clear. The therapist should understand and execute it. The leader should follow up appropriately. The therapist should take accountability for the outcome.

At Zura Spa, task assignment should never be about simply keeping staff busy. Every task should contribute to the smooth operation, cleanliness, teamwork, service quality, and overall standard of the spa.
LEADERS: GIVE CLARITY. THERAPISTS: TAKE OWNERSHIP. TOGETHER: GET THE JOB DONE.

remember: Leaders give clarity. Therapists take ownership. Together, get the job done.
